_comment: Single source of truth for the software apps shipped by this monorepo. Consumed by scripts/build_site.py (GitHub Pages landing page + deploy copy list) and scripts/publish_portfolio.py (portfolio cards + Obsidian notes). `summary` is the one-line portfolio-card copy (HTML-ready, keep it under ~120 visible characters so cards stay even); `description` is the full copy shown in the card's Details view and the Obsidian note (HTML-ready); `desc` is the short landing-page blurb. Optional `portfolio_order` overrides `order` for the portfolio card sequence only (the lowest values are the featured cards shown first); `portfolio: false` keeps an app off the portfolio without changing the landing page or notes. `links` are relative to the deployed site root (https://juw12.github.io/projects/<rel>). Extra fields `image_alt`, `project_id`, `label` (thumbnail aria-label) and `desc` reproduce the live markup verbatim. Card art (`image`, in the portfolio's assets/projects) must be house style: a 1600x1000 live-UI screenshot framed in the standard browser window on the dark accent gradient. Make it with `python scripts/portfolio_card.py <id>` (optional per-app `card` object: capture, frame_image, click, wait_ms, label, theme, accent, accent2) and never hand-draw, halftone or paste raw screenshots; publish_portfolio.py refuses cards that are missing, undersized or greyscale.

apps.description: Twin is an iPhone-ready investing and trading companion with a clean, professional design (1.5.1: new design system, line icons, dark and light themes) that tells you when a new version is ready and installs it in one tap. New in 1.15: the Twin desktop app for Windows and Mac — your own Twin server and app in one program, so real trading with Alpaca or Interactive Brokers needs no Python or terminal — and Add money: see your broker cash and buying power, follow a step-by-step deposit at your broker and get told when the money arrives (Twin never holds your money). From 1.13: two wallets, one picture — move practice money between your US dollar portfolio and the Twin Indonesia rupiah wallet at the delayed mid rate minus a 0.5% practice spread; both ledgers update together (in one revision-checked request on your own server, or in this browser on the web demo), moved money counts as money put in so returns stay honest, and Portfolio and Me show both wallets and the combined total. From 1.12: the Twin Indonesia rupiah wallet shows on Home and Me, syncs to your Twin account on your own server (conflict-safe across devices), and Indonesian, crypto and gold headlines come from every feed through the server or refresh hourly on the web demo. From 1.11: Twin Indonesia, the rupiah side of Twin at twin/id/ — IDX stocks in 100-share lots with price steps and broker fees, US stocks at the shown USD/IDR rate, crypto and gold priced in rupiah, community rooms with Scam Shield, an Analyst Desk whose ideas are scored against real prices, and nine interactive lessons, with a separate rupiah practice wallet. From 1.10: a premium landing page and the premium look on every tab — glowing portfolio card on Invest, gradient academy and colourful course tiles on Learn, rounded Trade and News cards, and a big avatar header on Me. From 1.9: a premium dark design with a glowing balance hero, quick actions, swipeable cards and a Buy/Sell dock on every stock. From 1.8: big bold numbers, soft borderless cards, pill buttons, coloured ticker badges, a floating glass tab bar, charts that draw themselves in, count-up portfolio value and swipe-to-close sheets. New in 1.7: real-time prices from your own Interactive Brokers, Alpaca or Finnhub account with the source shown on every stock page (Yahoo stays the labelled, delayed fallback), a read-only IBKR gateway self-test, Qatar and Abu Dhabi holiday calendars, daily backups of your data and a safe updater. From 1.6: the web demo covers about 280 stocks and ETFs on 35+ exchanges plus 34 indices, refreshed hourly; market status follows real exchange calendars (holidays, early closes); FX rates refresh every minute with their time shown; and real orders can go through Interactive Brokers for world exchanges as well as Alpaca for US listings. From 1.5: TwinAgent, a free research team of five analysts (trend, SEC-filed fundamentals, risk, relevance-screened headlines, famous investors' 13Fs) that argue a bull and bear case from cited, dated evidence; a portfolio manager rates the stock and a risk gate built from your own limits sizes or blocks the idea. No AI subscription, the same evidence always gives the same report, future data is filtered out, and a walk-forward scorecard tests the price evidence over decades against buy-and-hold. Search stocks by company, ticker or country — Tokyo, Hong Kong, Jakarta, London, Frankfurt, Mumbai, Toronto, São Paulo, Sydney and more — with exchange, currency, market status and next holidays, ≈ USD price with the FX time and US-listing hints on every stock page. World markets shows market clocks, 34 indices, movers and a heatmap; practice trades in a separate $10,000 USD portfolio convert foreign prices at current FX rates, and totals can be shown in your home currency (25 currencies). Continue as guest or share a ?guest link; market, limit, stop, stop-limit and trailing orders with brackets, price alerts, scrub charts with SMA/EMA/RSI, portfolio X-ray with country and currency exposure, a bar-by-bar Replay Lab and 12 Twin Academy lessons. The local server searches any Yahoo Finance listing; the web demo uses an hourly snapshot of about 280 global stocks and ETFs. Optional real trading on the local server through your own Alpaca (US) or Interactive Brokers (world exchanges) account, with preview, confirm, caps and submission-time checks. Not financial advice.

apps.desc: One app for money and spreadsheets: a live, end-to-end encrypted shared budget with a money-personality plan, limit warnings and a portfolio, a Marketplace tab to buy, generate and sell budget plans, investing mixes and Excel / Google Sheets templates with instant checkout on the seller's own Midtrans, Xendit or Stripe; many currencies with daily rates, an investing quiz, tips and regional money news, one encrypted account that syncs every device, and expense logging by WhatsApp chat (sealed so only your devices can read it); asks your language and region first; free on Windows, Mac, Android, iPhone and the web
apps.summary: Shared budgets in any currency, synced on every device. Log expenses by WhatsApp, plus a template Marketplace.
apps.description: Mint is one app with two halves. Budget is a budget you share like a Google Sheet, with an interface built only for money: a 30-second setup turns take-home pay into needs / wants / savings / investing envelopes, an optional 2-minute quiz assigns one of six money personalities, a live sheet with cell-level merging, warnings at 80%, over the limit or when your pace will overspend (including when someone else's edit tips a category), goals and an investing portfolio with drift and rebalancing. Sharing is local-first and end-to-end encrypted (AES-GCM, key in the link fragment) over ntfy.sh or a self-hostable stdlib relay, with no account. Templates is a live marketplace for Excel / Google Sheets templates: describe a sheet in English or Bahasa Indonesia and Mint AI designs it, tweak it with words (“add column Supplier”), export a real .xlsx with live formulas and a dashboard, then sell it — buyers pay the seller directly through the seller's own Midtrans, Xendit or Stripe checkout (QRIS, e-wallets, VA, cards) or a payment link, with coupons, tracked affiliate commissions, seller insights and Web Push notifications, on a Cloudflare Workers + SQLite Durable Object backend. Since 3.2, expenses, income and holdings can be in any currency and are converted to the budget's currency with daily exchange rates (the original amount is kept); Invest adds a 12-question quiz, personal tips and regional money news; the template studio lives inside Mint as a Marketplace tab where you can also sell your own budget plan or investing mix (shares of income only, never real amounts) and buyers see prices in their own currency; and one Mint account keeps budgets in sync on every device, encrypted on the device before upload (PBKDF2 + AES-GCM, with a recovery code). WhatsApp: text Mint what you spent (“coffee 25k”, “grab 18rb”, “lunch 12 usd yesterday”, “+5jt salary”, several per message) and it lands in your budget, categorised like Quick add and converted from any currency, with undo from the chat. Each message is sealed on arrival to a key only your signed-in devices hold (ECDH P-256 + AES-GCM), so the Cloudflare Worker never stores anything it can read; WhatsApp logging is rolling out as Mint's WhatsApp Business number goes live. The first time it opens, Mint asks for a language (English, Bahasa Indonesia, 简体中文 or Español) and a region, and the region sets the currency of new budgets and templates. Both halves share one install, one icon, one light / dark / system theme and that one language (Templates is in English and Bahasa Indonesia), and update themselves in place. Free as a Windows and Mac desktop app, an Android app, an iPhone home-screen app and on the web; the desktop and Android builds are opened and checked on their own systems before every release. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step.

apps.name: Photo2CAD
apps.desc: Turn a product PRD plus six reference photos into a real STEP (.stp) CAD model - an LLM writes a CadQuery program, a sandbox builds the solid and the server validates it
apps.description: Engineering service that turns a product requirements document (PRD) and six reference photographs (front/back/left/right/top/bottom) into a real CAD file. A Pegatron MAAS LLM writes a parametric CadQuery program from the PRD (the photos are visual/dimension reference), a sandboxed child process builds it, and the server re-imports the STEP to validate a single solid with its bounding box and volume - returning a downloadable .stp plus an STL preview. Ships as a deployable web service (Docker + Kubernetes). Output is STEP; Creo .prt is proprietary and not produced (Creo imports STEP).
apps.summary: PRD + six reference photos to a validated STEP (.stp) CAD model via an LLM-written CadQuery program - a deployable service.
apps.image_alt: photo2cad workbench: a PRD editor and six reference-photo slots beside a CAD viewport

apps.name: shiphub
apps.desc: Pinterest for app ideas with forum threads: save ideas to boards, discuss them, fork them, claim one and mark it shipped with repo and demo links
apps.summary: Pinterest for app ideas with forum threads: save, discuss, fork, claim and ship ideas, with GitHub sign-in.
apps.description: shiphub is a pinboard of app ideas worth vibe-coding, with a forum built in. Ideas show up as a masonry feed (Hot, New, Top, Discussed; filter by Up for grabs, Building or Shipped; tags and live search). Each idea has a threaded discussion with votes, a fork button to remix it, and builders: hit “I'm building this”, then mark it shipped with a repo and demo link. Save ideas to boards, get notifications for replies, builds and forks, and copy any idea as a ready-to-paste AI prompt. Accounts with passwords or GitHub sign-in, cover and profile-photo uploads, moderators, rate limits and a strict content security policy. The server is plain Python (no dependencies) on SQLite, or Postgres for hosting, with Docker, Render and Fly.io configs.
apps.image_alt: shiphub feed: a dark masonry board of app-idea cards with Hot, New, Top and Discussed tabs and tag chips

apps.name: Sortie
apps.desc: Playful file organizer: files fly into folders, a vacuum sucks up deletes, and an AI assistant plans moves, renames and cleanups
apps.summary: File organizer with fly-into-folder animations, a vacuum for deletes and an AI assistant that plans before it acts.
apps.description: Sortie is a file organizer styled as a Google Drive × macOS Finder hybrid. Sorted files fly into their folders, and deleted files get sucked up by a vacuum cleaner into a recoverable Vacuum bag. Finder-style sidebar with Favorites, Folders and Tags, Drive-style filter chips and selection bar, icon and striped list views, back/forward history and a path bar. An AI assistant (offline rule-based helper, or OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Ollama and LM Studio) turns plain requests such as “vacuum duplicates” into a plan you Run or Cancel; everything is undoable. Works on real folders in Chrome and Edge via the File System Access API, with demo and preview modes that never touch the disk. Installable PWA, light and dark themes, no build step.
apps.image_alt: Sortie file organizer: Finder-style sidebar with folders and tags, Drive-style search and filter chips, and a grid of files

apps.name: KiniBuka
apps.desc: Stall discovery for Indonesian UMKM: live open/closed status, branches, bazaars, map, follow alerts and order-ahead with a WhatsApp handoff
apps.summary: Find UMKM stalls open right now: live status, branches, bazaars, map, follow alerts and order-ahead via WhatsApp.
apps.description: KiniBuka (“now open”) helps people find small Indonesian food and retail stalls that are open right now. A live feed shows openings, closings, new branches, promos and bazaars; Explore combines search, category filters and an OpenStreetMap map. Buyers follow stalls to get alerts and order ahead with a pickup time, tracking it from accepted to ready to done, with one-tap WhatsApp buttons to chat with the seller. Sellers get a dashboard to toggle open/closed, manage branches, menu and promos, run bazaars and handle incoming orders, with optional WhatsApp auto-notifications through Fonnte or the Meta Cloud API. Interface in Bahasa Indonesia, English and 中文. Plain Python server (no dependencies) on SQLite.
apps.image_alt: KiniBuka on three phone screens: a live feed of stalls opening and closing, an Explore map with search, and a stall page with menu and order-ahead

apps.name: Rewind
apps.desc: Community archive for old TV series missing from today's streaming platforms: memories, quotes, availability status, shelves and a live feed
apps.summary: Remember the shows streaming forgot: share memories and quotes, track where a series can still be watched.
apps.description: Rewind is a community archive for old TV series that are hard to find on today’s streaming platforms. Browse the archive as poster tiles with search, decade and availability filters; each series opens a panel with memories, quotes, “I remember this” counts and a community availability status (not streaming, partial, physical media only, streaming). Keep favourites on My Shelf and follow new posts in Memory Lane. A full Settings page covers day/night mode (System, Light, Dark), accent colour, text size, card density, reduce motion, start page, default sort, hiding shows that are already streaming, and export/import of the archive. Every page and series has a shareable link and the back button closes panels. Runs local-first in the browser, or online with Supabase (magic-link sign-in, row-level security, realtime feed). Installable PWA, no build step.
apps.image_alt: Rewind archive in dark mode: a grid of series poster tiles with search, decade and availability filters

apps.name: ScopeGuard
apps.desc: Keeps a business AI assistant on its mission: allows on-topic requests, steers related ones, redirects off-topic use and blocks jailbreaks
apps.summary: Stop users turning your business AI into a free ChatGPT: allow, steer, redirect or block every message.
apps.description: ScopeGuard sits between your users and your AI assistant and keeps it on its mission. Every message gets one of five decisions: allow on-mission requests, answer related ones briefly and steer back, redirect off-topic use without ever calling the LLM, throttle repeat offenders after a daily allowance, and block jailbreaks and prompt injection. The app runs the guard entirely in the browser: chat as different users, simulate traffic, and watch a dashboard of off-mission share, estimated LLM cost avoided, unmet-demand themes and flagged users. A review queue teaches the classifier instantly. Edit, import and export policies, with templates for a CAD copilot, a bank and an online store. An Accuracy page measures it on held-out test sets (85% served-vs-stopped on a never-tuned set) or your own cases. For production, the same engine ships as a self-hosted, standard-library Python server with a check API and an OpenAI-compatible proxy.
apps.image_alt: ScopeGuard dashboard in dark mode: decisions, unmet-demand themes, flagged users and a review queue

apps.name: CrewCup
apps.desc: Office coffee for teams in Indonesia and SEA: solo or group coffee runs, company allowance, badge pickup at partner cafés and rewards
apps.summary: Office coffee for teams: one-tap usual, group runs, company allowance, badge pickup at partner cafés and rewards.
apps.description: CrewCup is office coffee for teams in Indonesia and Southeast Asia. Employees order their usual in one tap or join a group coffee run with a cutoff (everyone's share is held, so the runner never pays upfront), paid from the company allowance, then pick up at a partner café with their company badge QR. Cafés get an order board batched by pickup slot, cup labels with allergy warnings, stock, payouts and catering; HR gets budgets, spend and tax receipts, runner fairness and an audit log. Includes company rewards (send a coffee, nominations), a loyalty program with points, tiers, coupons, café offers and achievements, and the CrewCup Network to meet other companies in your building. QRIS-style top-ups, live updates, English and Bahasa Indonesia. Plain Python server (no dependencies) on SQLite, 101 tests.
apps.image_alt: CrewCup home screen: greeting, Order my usual button, allowance, wallet, points and badge tiles, and personal suggestions

apps.name: Haru
apps.desc: Cozy photo diary, walking map and weather town for phone and desktop: a weather-lit diorama for each day, a walk map and a screenshot tidy-up
apps.summary: Your days as a cozy little town: a weather-lit diorama, photo, note and walk for each day, plus a screenshot tidy-up.
apps.description: Haru is a calm photo diary, walking map and weather town in a cozy Japanese/Korean indie style. Each day becomes a card: a tiny street-corner diorama lit by that day’s real weather and time (192 pre-rendered scenes), a polaroid photo, a short note, a hanko mood stamp and the distance you walked, with new streets marked on your personal walk map. On-this-day memories, random fragments and gentle daily prompts bring old days back. A screenshot tidy-up swipes through your screenshots (keep, let go, later), reads them on the device with OCR in Japanese, Korean and English, sorts them into drawers (tickets, receipts, recipes, places, chats), finds duplicates and flags expiring tickets. Four language modes: Japanese and Korean side by side, English, Japanese or Korean. Use it now in any browser (installable on iPhone via Add to Home Screen), or download it for Android, Windows and Mac; the native SwiftUI iPhone app (SwiftData, WeatherKit, PhotoKit, Vision, widgets) builds and is tested on CI.
apps.image_alt: Haru swipe deck: a day card with a tiny 3D street-corner diorama in autumn light, a cat polaroid, a short note and a hanko mood stamp

apps.name: Buddy
apps.desc: An AI pointer that lives next to your mouse: ask about your screen and it points at the answer, explains it aloud or does it for you
apps.summary: AI buddy next to your mouse: hold Ctrl+Alt+Space, ask about your screen, and it points at the answer or does it for you.
apps.description: A small orange pointer rests next to your mouse. Hold Ctrl+Alt+Space and ask out loud (or tap it to type): Buddy looks once at the screen under your mouse, flies to the exact button, explains it in a speech bubble and reads it aloud in a natural, on-device voice (7 languages). If your words ask for it, it clicks, types, opens, closes and presses shortcuts for you, asks Yes/No before anything risky, and writes every action to a log. Pick the brain: a fast vision model on any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or Local GPU / CPU so nothing leaves the PC. The pointer runs on its own thread and window, so it keeps up even on a busy laptop. Pick its colour and icon. Bundles the Pips focus pet and KeyIt keyboard and mouse sounds. Buddy Lite for Mac (Control+Option+Space, one universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel) points and answers with Apple speech recognition and system voices; it is built and self-tested on real macOS by GitHub Actions. Free, MIT, no installer and no account.
apps.image_alt: Buddy pointing at File, Save As in Notepad with a speech bubble that says Right here

apps.name: EarlyStar
apps.desc: Find GitHub repos before they trend: ranked by stars actually gained, with real activity next to the hype
apps.summary: Find GitHub repos before they trend: ranked by stars actually gained, with real activity, Trending history and a free API.
apps.description: EarlyStar finds GitHub repositories before they trend. Instead of total stars it ranks repos by the stars they actually gained, and puts real activity next to the hype so a breakout is easy to tell from a spike. It keeps a GitHub Trending history and offers embeddable badges, a free JSON API and a desktop app.
apps.image_alt: EarlyStar leaderboard of GitHub repositories ranked by stars gained, with activity columns

apps.name: Together
apps.desc: Life plan for couples — roadmap from dating to golden years, goals, money, check-ins. Encrypted partner sync, reminders, offline
apps.description: A private life-planning app for couples. Roadmap: 10 life stages from dating to golden years with both partners' ages on every milestone. Goals with steps. Money: savings pots linked to milestones, a retirement planner with inflation and fees, education funds and a net-worth tracker. Us: monthly check-ins, “talk before you decide” topics and an 8-week Foundations program summarising Gottman and PREP research. One plan on both phones via end-to-end-encrypted sync (key only in the pairing link), push reminders, installable and offline.
apps.summary: Couples' life plan: roadmap with both ages, goals, money, check-ins. Encrypted partner sync, reminders, offline.
